name: Dhamma Visuddhi
tradition: Vipassana Meditation as taught by S.N. Goenka, in the tradition of Sayagyi U Ba Khin
technique: Anapana and Vipassana body-scan meditation, taught step-by-step in silent, fixed-schedule residential courses
teacherAccess: No individual dharma talks; a certified assistant teacher is on-site to answer technique questions during a daily interview period (12-1pm) and public question time (9-9:30pm); nightly discourse is a recorded video/audio talk by S.N. Goenka.
retreatOptions: Standard 10-day residential courses (most common offering), plus periodic 3-day and short old-student courses for those who have already completed a 10-day course.
schedule: Fixed daily timetable from 4:00am wake-up to 9:30pm lights-out, with alternating group and self-directed meditation sessions, meal breaks, and an evening video discourse; Noble Silence is observed by all students until the morning of the last full day.
cost: No tuition fee of any kind; entirely dana (voluntary donation)-based. First-time students may donate at the end of the course if they wish; only returning students who have completed a prior course may donate toward future courses.

pricePerDay.notes: No suggested amount; first-time students give only after completing a course.

foodNotes: Simple vegetarian meals prepared and served on-site for the full duration of the course; special dietary requests generally cannot be accommodated except for medically documented conditions.
workNotes: New students are not required to work during their first course; returning ("old") students are invited to volunteer as course servers or to attend dedicated service periods that help run and maintain the center.
about: Dhamma Visuddhi is a Vipassana meditation center on 15 forested acres overlooking the Red Cedar River in Menomonie, Wisconsin, about an hour east of the Minneapolis-St. Paul airport. Established in 2013, it is one of the Goenka tradition's roughly 16 centers in North America, offering the standard 10-day residential Vipassana course taught via recorded instruction from S.N. Goenka along with on-site assistant teachers. Students live on the dorm-style campus for the full course, observe Noble Silence for most of the stay, and follow a fixed daily meditation schedule. Courses run entirely on voluntary donations from past students, with no set fees for anyone attending their first course. A 19th-century mansion houses the kitchen, dining halls, and some student lodging, with separate dormitory buildings for men and women elsewhere on the property.
